chunks: And it is narrated from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated to us, who said: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say:

Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) in the month of Ramadan and dies on the route, will not be presented [with his book of deeds], will not be held to account, and it will be said to him, 'Enter Paradise in safety.'

key_terms.لَمْ يُحَاسَبْ: will not be held to account

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for dying while traveling to visit Imam Husayn's grave in Ramadan?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the unique merit of combining the devotion of Ramadan with the pilgrimage to the Ahl al-Bayt, elevating the status of the visitor to one of immediate entry into Paradise. The phrase 'not presented and not reckoned' (lam yu'rad wa la yuhasab) signifies a special dispensation from the detailed accounting of deeds, reflecting the intercessory power of Imam al-Husayn's shrine. This highlights the theological concept that sincere devotion to the Imams can serve as a means of divine mercy and direct salvation.
